facts.fact: The authors say Law No. 2024/017 Relating to Personal Data Protection of 23 December 2024 becomes enforceable after an 18-month grace period from enactment.

facts.fact: The authors say the Personal Data Protection Authority provided for in the Act is yet to be established.
Professor Jean Louis Fendji said at a CENADI workshop that Cameroon has no data protection law yet.
The document says Cameroon signed the Malabo Convention on 12 August 2021 and that ratification is awaited.

CLG Global reports the compliance transition period under Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on personal data protection closed on 23 June 2026, and says operators should assume its obligations apply now.
CLG Global says the data protection authority under Law No. 2024/017 is not yet operational and awaits its presidential decree, so no head or members are appointed.

facts.fact: ACTPOL says Cameroon's Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 gave organisations 18 months to comply, a period that ended on 23 June 2026.
ACTPOL, citing the African Union status list of 2 February 2026, says Cameroon has signed the Malabo Convention without ratifying it.
ACTPOL says it found no decree creating Cameroon's Personal Data Protection Authority as of July 2026.
Levellers says Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on personal data protection is in force, with enforceability after a grace period ending 23 June 2026.
facts.system: Law No. 2024/017 on personal data protection

facts.fact: Levellers says that per the AU status list Cameroon has signed the Malabo Convention without ratifying it.
Levellers says the Personal Data Protection Authority had not been created by presidential decree or made operational as of mid-2026.
